chapter: Los Angeles, Central Avenue and the Apex
title: Boyhood chores and community values compared with today
summary: Royal contrasts neighborhood discipline and working for everything with the looser upbringing of today's children.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: We -- when I was a kid, I always liked to get out and see what was happening with the other kids around the neighborhood. I never really had a paper route of my own or we called them routes in those days, routes probably, but we called them paper routes. I'd get up at 3:00 in the morning just to be with my friends and I'd go out and help them throw their papers before daybreak, before time for school, just to be a part of the gang. In those days, that's what we sort of thought it was all about, being one of the guys. Today, the camaraderie is so much different. Everybody's for themselves. Guys is looking to, in this young kids now, looking to find out how they can cheat their fellow man rather than helping him and do something for him.

It was so much more fun, I think, in the days where we had to work for everything that we got. All the kids in the neighborhood and the families, they had chores of some type that they had to do, because a lot of the families' mothers and fathers were out doing day work and every other kind of work that they could do to try to help make things meet. And Everybody had something lined out for them to do, kept them out of mischief and sort of helped to give a pure sense of values to

what life was really all about. Family ties were much closer and there was more love thrown around. Any guy that was out on the street and did something wrong, if one of the neighbors, the grown-up neighbors, happened to see him, he'd get a spanking right then from the neighbor and then, when the father would come home from work, the neighbor would tell the father what had happened and he'd get another one when the father came home.

Nowadays, if a teacher in school paddles a child, they get drawn before the courts for child molesting and child brutality and all of that sort of thing. The whole upbringing the kids now is so loose that it sort of changes the values of the young people coming up. I don't think it's very nice.
